section_1.title: Prerequisite: The Bernoulli Trial
section_1.content: Introduce the foundation of binomial distributions: the Bernoulli Trial. Define it as a single experiment with exactly two outcomes: Success or Failure. Explain that the probability of success (p) must remain constant.
section_1.example: Pip the Penguin is trying to catch a fish. He either catches it (Success, p=0.7) or he doesn't (Failure, q=0.3). This single attempt is a Bernoulli trial.

section_2.title: Defining the Binomial Distribution (The BINS Criteria)
section_2.content: Transition from one trial to multiple trials. Introduce the four essential conditions for a Binomial Distribution using the acronym BINS: Binary (Success/Failure), Independent trials, fixed Number of trials (n), and Same probability of success (p).
section_2.example: Pip makes 10 independent fishing attempts. Animation shows 10 slots filling with either a fish icon or an 'X'. This sequence follows the BINS criteria.

section_3.title: Visualizing the Probability Tree
section_3.content: Explain why we need a formula. Use a small-scale tree diagram to show how different paths lead to the same number of successes. This visualizes the concept of 'combinations'—the number of ways to get k successes in n trials.
section_3.example: If Pip tries 3 times, how many ways can he catch exactly 2 fish? Visual: A tree diagram branching out. Path 1: (S,S,F), Path 2: (S,F,S), Path 3: (F,S,S). Total = 3 ways.

section_4.title: Deconstructing the Binomial Formula
section_4.content: Present the formula: P(X=k) = nCk * p^k * (1-p)^(n-k). Use color-coding to link the formula parts to the logic: nCk (the number of paths), p^k (probability of successes), and (1-p)^(n-k) (probability of failures).
section_4.example: An animated graphic highlights n=10, k=7. It shows 10C7 calculating the 'arrangements', 0.7^7 for the fish caught, and 0.3^3 for the misses, then multiplying them together.

section_5.title: Visualizing the Distribution Shape
section_5.content: Show a dynamic bar chart (Probability Mass Function). Demonstrate how changing 'n' (number of trials) and 'p' (probability) alters the shape. Explain that as 'n' increases, the distribution looks more like a bell curve (Normal approximation).
section_5.example: Interactive slider animation: When p=0.5, the bars are perfectly symmetrical. When p=0.1, the bars pile up on the left (Skewed Right). Watch the graph shift as Pip's skill level (p) improves.

section_6.title: Real-World Application: Quality Control
section_6.content: Apply the concept to a practical scenario to solidify understanding. Show how businesses use this to predict risks or outcomes.
section_6.example: A robot arm assembles 50 gadgets. Each gadget has a 2% chance of being defective. Using the binomial distribution, we calculate the probability that the batch contains more than 3 defects, helping the factory manage quality.

outline.title: Defining the Binomial Distribution (The BINS Criteria)
outline.content: Transition from one trial to multiple trials. Introduce the four essential conditions for a Binomial Distribution using the acronym BINS: Binary (Success/Failure), Independent trials, fixed Number of trials (n), and Same probability of success (p).
outline.example: Pip makes 10 independent fishing attempts. Animation shows 10 slots filling with either a fish icon or an 'X'. This sequence follows the BINS criteria.

outline.title: Deconstructing the Binomial Formula
outline.content: Present the formula: P(X=k) = nCk * p^k * (1-p)^(n-k). Use color-coding to link the formula parts to the logic: nCk (the number of paths), p^k (probability of successes), and (1-p)^(n-k) (probability of failures).
outline.example: An animated graphic highlights n=10, k=7. It shows 10C7 calculating the 'arrangements', 0.7^7 for the fish caught, and 0.3^3 for the misses, then multiplying them together.

Number: The total number of trials is fixed.
Success: The probability of success remains constant.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(f"- {line}", font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT, buff=0.4).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1.1  # Shifted to the right side
                y = 2.5 - i * 1.0
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: The Bernoulli Trial", [
            "A Bernoulli trial has only two possible outcomes.",
            "We label these results as Success or Failure.",

        # Target the p=0.7 part of the success label
        # Since it's a Text object, we find the specific characters or just flash the whole label

        p_label_highlight = Text("p=0.7", color=YELLOW, font_size=24)
        p_label_highlight.move_to(success_label.get_center())
        
        self.play(Flash(success_label, color=YELLOW, flash_radius=0.5))
        self.play(success_label.animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.wait(2)

            "This shape represents the most likely outcomes."
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)
        
        # Define constants and trackers
        chart_color = "#ADD8E6"
        highlight_color = YELLOW
        n_tracker = ValueTracker(10)
        p_tracker = ValueTracker(0.5)
        
        # Create Axes
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 31, 5],
            y_range=[0, 0.5, 0.1],
            x_length=5,
            y_length=4,

        y_label.next_to(axes.y_axis, LEFT, buff=0.4)

        for i in range(31):

                stroke_width=0.5,

            n = int(n_tracker.get_value())
            p = p_tracker.get_value()
            for i, b in enumerate(m):
                if i <= n:
                    # Binomial PMF: (n choose i) * p^i * (1-p)^(n-i)
                    try:
                        prob = math.comb(n, i) * (p**i) * ((1-p)**(n-i))
                    except:
                        prob = 0
                    
                    # Convert probability to visual height
                    target_height = axes.c2p(0, prob)[1] - axes.c2p(0, 0)[1]

            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(highlight_color),
            p_tracker.animate.set_value(0.2),
            Write(skew_right_label),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        skew_left_label = Text("Skewed Left", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(skew_left_label, 'B2', scale_factor=1.0)

            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(highlight_color),
            p_tracker.animate.set_value(0.8),
            ReplacementTransform(skew_right_label, skew_left_label),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(highlight_color),
            p_tracker.animate.set_value(0.5),
            n_tracker.animate.set_value(30),
            FadeOut(skew_left_label),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===

        highest_bar = bars[15]
        
        self.play(
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(highlight_color),

from manim import *
import math

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)

        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2

        mobject.move_to(center)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Fetching data from storyboard
        title_text = "Visualizing the Distribution Shape"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Probability mass functions show the distribution of results.",
            "When p is low, the graph skews right.",
            "As p increases, the peak shifts to the right.",
            "High trial counts create a symmetric bell curve.",
            "This shape represents the most likely outcomes."
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)
        
        # Define constants and trackers
        chart_color = "#ADD8E6"
        highlight_color = YELLOW
        n_tracker = ValueTracker(10)
        p_tracker = ValueTracker(0.5)
        
        # Create Axes
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 31, 5],
            y_range=[0, 0.5, 0.1],
            x_length=5,
            y_length=4,
            axis_config={"include_tip": False}
        ).add_coordinates(font_size=14)
        self.place_in_area(axes, 'A1', 'F6', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Axis Labels
        x_label = Text("Number of Successes (k)", font_size=16, color=WHITE)
        x_label.next_to(axes.x_axis, DOWN, buff=0.4)
        y_label = Text("P(X=k)", font_size=16, color=WHITE).rotate(90*DEGREES)
        y_label.next_to(axes.y_axis, LEFT, buff=0.4)
        
        self.add(axes, x_label, y_label)

        # Create Bars
        # Initialize 31 bars to accommodate n up to 30
        bars = VGroup()
        for i in range(31):
            bar = Rectangle(
                width=0.12,
                height=0.01,
                fill_opacity=0.8,
                fill_color=chart_color,
                stroke_width=0.5,
                stroke_color=WHITE
            )
            bar.move_to(axes.c2p(i, 0), aligned_edge=DOWN)
            bars.add(bar)
            
        def update_bars(m):
            n = int(n_tracker.get_value())
            p = p_tracker.get_value()
            for i, b in enumerate(m):
                if i <= n:
                    # Binomial PMF: (n choose i) * p^i * (1-p)^(n-i)
                    try:
                        prob = math.comb(n, i) * (p**i) * ((1-p)**(n-i))
                    except:
                        prob = 0
                    
                    # Convert probability to visual height
                    target_height = axes.c2p(0, prob)[1] - axes.c2p(0, 0)[1]
                    # Update height using stretch_to_fit_height for performance
                    b.stretch_to_fit_height(max(target_height, 0.001))
                    b.move_to(axes.c2p(i, 0), aligned_edge=DOWN)
                    b.set_opacity(0.8)
                else:
                    b.set_opacity(0)
                    
        bars.add_updater(update_bars)
        self.add(bars)

        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(highlight_color))
        self.wait(2)

        self.place_at_grid(skew_right_label, 'B5', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(highlight_color),
            p_tracker.animate.set_value(0.2),
            Write(skew_right_label),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        skew_left_label = Text("Skewed Left", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(skew_left_label, 'B2', scale_factor=1.0)

        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(highlight_color),
            p_tracker.animate.set_value(0.8),
            ReplacementTransform(skew_right_label, skew_left_label),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(highlight_color),
            p_tracker.animate.set_value(0.5),
            n_tracker.animate.set_value(30),
            FadeOut(skew_left_label),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # For n=30, p=0.5, the mode is 15.
        highest_bar = bars[15]
        
        self.play(
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(highlight_color),
        )
        self.play(Flash(highest_bar, color=YELLOW, flash_radius=0.5, line_length=0.3))
        self.wait(2)
        
        # End state cleanup
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(1)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)

section_1.title: Prerequisite: The Bernoulli Trial
section_1.content: Introduce the foundation of binomial distributions: the Bernoulli Trial. Define it as a single experiment with exactly two outcomes: Success or Failure. Explain that the probability of success (p) must remain constant.
section_1.example: Pip the Penguin is trying to catch a fish. He either catches it (Success, p=0.7) or he doesn't (Failure, q=0.3). This single attempt is a Bernoulli trial.

section_2.title: Defining the Binomial Distribution (The BINS Criteria)
section_2.content: Transition from one trial to multiple trials. Introduce the four essential conditions for a Binomial Distribution using the acronym BINS: Binary (Success/Failure), Independent trials, fixed Number of trials (n), and Same probability of success (p).
section_2.example: Pip makes 10 independent fishing attempts. Animation shows 10 slots filling with either a fish icon or an 'X'. This sequence follows the BINS criteria.

section_3.title: Visualizing the Probability Tree
section_3.content: Explain why we need a formula. Use a small-scale tree diagram to show how different paths lead to the same number of successes. This visualizes the concept of 'combinations'—the number of ways to get k successes in n trials.
section_3.example: If Pip tries 3 times, how many ways can he catch exactly 2 fish? Visual: A tree diagram branching out. Path 1: (S,S,F), Path 2: (S,F,S), Path 3: (F,S,S). Total = 3 ways.

section_4.title: Deconstructing the Binomial Formula
section_4.content: Present the formula: P(X=k) = nCk * p^k * (1-p)^(n-k). Use color-coding to link the formula parts to the logic: nCk (the number of paths), p^k (probability of successes), and (1-p)^(n-k) (probability of failures).
section_4.example: An animated graphic highlights n=10, k=7. It shows 10C7 calculating the 'arrangements', 0.7^7 for the fish caught, and 0.3^3 for the misses, then multiplying them together.

section_5.title: Visualizing the Distribution Shape
section_5.content: Show a dynamic bar chart (Probability Mass Function). Demonstrate how changing 'n' (number of trials) and 'p' (probability) alters the shape. Explain that as 'n' increases, the distribution looks more like a bell curve (Normal approximation).
section_5.example: Interactive slider animation: When p=0.5, the bars are perfectly symmetrical. When p=0.1, the bars pile up on the left (Skewed Right). Watch the graph shift as Pip's skill level (p) improves.

section_6.title: Real-World Application: Quality Control
section_6.content: Apply the concept to a practical scenario to solidify understanding. Show how businesses use this to predict risks or outcomes.
section_6.example: A robot arm assembles 50 gadgets. Each gadget has a 2% chance of being defective. Using the binomial distribution, we calculate the probability that the batch contains more than 3 defects, helping the factory manage quality.

lecture_lines: A Bernoulli trial has only two possible outcomes.
We label these results as Success or Failure.
The probability of success must stay the same.
animations: Show a card labeled 'Bernoulli Trial' in the center of the screen in white #FFFFFF.
Split the screen: left side shows a fish icon [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/fish.svg] 'Success (p=0.7)' in green #00FF00, right side shows 'Failure (q=0.3)' in red #FF0000.
Flash the 'p=0.7' label in yellow #FFFF00 to emphasize that the probability remains constant.

section_2.title: Defining the Binomial Distribution (The BINS Criteria)
lecture_lines: Binomial distributions follow the BINS criteria.
Binary: Each trial has only two outcomes.
Independent: One trial does not affect another.
Number: The total number of trials is fixed.
Success: The probability of success remains constant.
animations: Display the word 'BINS' in large white letters #FFFFFF at the top.
List 'Binary, Independent, Number, Same p' below 'BINS' in light blue #ADD8E6.
Show 10 slots filling sequentially with fish or 'X' icons to illustrate fixed n and binary outcomes.

section_3.title: Visualizing the Probability Tree
lecture_lines: A tree diagram shows every possible path.
Each path represents a specific sequence of outcomes.
Multiple paths can lead to the same result.
animations: Draw a probability tree with 3 levels in white #FFFFFF.
Highlight three paths: (S,S,F), (S,F,S), and (F,S,S) in yellow #FFFF00.
Label each highlighted path as 'Successes = 2' in yellow #FFFF00.
Group these three paths with a bracket and label them '3 ways to get 2 [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/fish.svg]' in light blue #ADD8E6.
Show the text '3C2 = 3' appearing next to the bracket in light green #90EE90.

section_4.title: Deconstructing the Binomial Formula
lecture_lines: The binomial formula calculates the probability of success.
Combination n-C-k counts the number of valid paths.
p to the k represents the successes.
q to the n-minus-k represents the failures.
Multiply these parts to find the total probability.
animations: Display the full binomial formula P(X=k) = nCk * p^k * (1-p)^(n-k) in white #FFFFFF.
Highlight 'nCk' in light green #90EE90 and label it 'Number of Ways'.
Highlight 'p^k' in light blue #ADD8E6 and label it 'Success Prob'.
Highlight '(1-p)^(n-k)' in light coral #F08080 and label it 'Failure Prob'.
Substitute values n=10, k=7, p=0.7 into the highlighted formula parts.

section_5.title: Visualizing the Distribution Shape
lecture_lines: Probability mass functions show the distribution of results.
When p is low, the graph skews right.
As p increases, the peak shifts to the right.
High trial counts create a symmetric bell curve.
This shape represents the most likely outcomes.
animations: Create a bar chart representing a binomial distribution for n=10, p=0.5 in light blue #ADD8E6.
Animate the bars shifting left as p changes to 0.2, labeling it 'Skewed Right'.
Animate the bars shifting right as p changes to 0.8, labeling it 'Skewed Left'.
Increase n from 10 to 30 with p=0.5 and show the chart smoothing into a bell-like shape.
Flash the highest bar to indicate the mode or most likely outcome.

section_6.title: Real-World Application: Quality Control
lecture_lines: Binomial logic helps factories predict part defects.
We calculate the likelihood of exceeding failure limits.
Statistics ensures quality control in mass production.
animations: Display a robot arm icon [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/robot.svg] and a conveyor belt [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/con.svg] of gadgets in white #FFFFFF.
Show the parameters 'n=50, p=0.02' next to the conveyor belt in light blue #ADD8E6.
Highlight the area of a distribution graph where X > 3 in red #FF0000 to represent 'Defect Risk'.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: The Bernoulli Trial", [
            "A Bernoulli trial has only two possible outcomes.",
            "We label these results as Success or Failure.",
            "The probability of success must stay the same."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show a card labeled 'Bernoulli Trial' in the center of the screen in white #FFFFFF.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        
        card_rect = RoundedRectangle(corner_radius=0.2, width=4, height=2, color=WHITE)
        card_text = Text("Bernoulli Trial", color=WHITE, font_size=36)
        card = VGroup(card_rect, card_text)
        self.place_in_area(card, 'B2', 'E5', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(card))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Split the screen: left side shows a fish icon 'Success (p=0.7)' in green #00FF00, 
        # right side shows 'Failure (q=0.3)' in red #FF0000.
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        
        # Success side (Left part of grid)
        # Using a simple shape for fish icon since no asset was provided
        success_icon = Triangle(color=GREEN).rotate(-90*DEGREES)
        success_label = Text("Success (p=0.7)", color=GREEN, font_size=24)
        success_group = VGroup(success_icon, success_label).arrange(DOWN)
        self.place_in_area(success_group, 'B1', 'E3', scale_factor=0.9)
        
        # Failure side (Right part of grid)
        failure_icon = Cross(stroke_width=6, color=RED)
        failure_label = Text("Failure (q=0.3)", color=RED, font_size=24)
        failure_group = VGroup(failure_icon, failure_label).arrange(DOWN)
        self.place_in_area(failure_group, 'B4', 'E6', scale_factor=0.9)

        self.play(
            FadeOut(card),
            FadeIn(success_group),
            FadeIn(failure_group)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Flash the 'p=0.7' label in yellow #FFFF00 to emphasize that the probability remains constant.
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        # Target the p=0.7 part of the success label
        # Since it's a Text object, we find the specific characters or just flash the whole label
        # For simplicity and robustness in Manim, let's create a highlight for that label.
        p_label_highlight = Text("p=0.7", color=YELLOW, font_size=24)
        p_label_highlight.move_to(success_label.get_center())
        
        self.play(Flash(success_label, color=YELLOW, flash_radius=0.5))
        self.play(success_label.animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup layout
        title_text = "Defining the Binomial Distribution (The BINS Criteria)"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Binomial distributions follow the BINS criteria.",
            "Binary: Each trial has only two outcomes.",
            "Independent: One trial does not affect another.",
            "Number: The total number of trials is fixed.",
            "Success: The probability of success remains constant."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)
        
        # Colors
        COLOR_BINS = WHITE
        COLOR_LIST = "#ADD8E6"
        
        # Helper functions for icons to avoid asset dependency
        def get_fish():
            # A simple fish-like shape using triangles
            fish_body = Triangle(fill_opacity=1, color=BLUE_B).rotate(-PI/2).scale(0.15)
            fish_tail = Triangle(fill_opacity=1, color=BLUE_B).rotate(PI/2).scale(0.08).next_to(fish_body, LEFT, buff=-0.05)
            return VGroup(fish_body, fish_tail)

        def get_x():
            # An 'X' icon for failure
            return Text("X", color=RED, font_size=36)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Binomial distributions follow the BINS criteria.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(COLOR_BINS)
        bins_title = Text("BINS", font_size=72, color=COLOR_BINS)
        self.place_in_area(bins_title, "A2", "A5")
        self.play(Write(bins_title))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Binary: Each trial has only two outcomes.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(COLOR_LIST)
        binary_text = Text("Binary", font_size=32, color=COLOR_LIST)
        self.place_at_grid(binary_text, "B2")
        
        # Prepare slots for the fishing example (illustrating binary outcomes and fixed n)
        slots = VGroup(*[Square(side_length=0.7, color=WHITE) for _ in range(10)])
        for i, slot in enumerate(slots):
            row_idx = "D" if i < 5 else "E"
            col_idx = str((i % 5) + 1)
            self.place_at_grid(slot, f"{row_idx}{col_idx}")
            
        self.play(
            FadeIn(binary_text),
            Create(slots)
        )
        
        # Binary outcomes example: Fish (Success) or X (Failure)
        fish_ex = get_fish()
        x_ex = get_x()
        self.place_at_grid(fish_ex, "C2")
        self.place_at_grid(x_ex, "C3")
        
        self.play(FadeIn(fish_ex), FadeIn(x_ex))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Independent: One trial does not affect another.
        self.lecture[2].set_color(COLOR_LIST)
        independent_text = Text("Independent", font_size=32, color=COLOR_LIST)
        self.place_at_grid(independent_text, "B3")
        self.play(FadeIn(independent_text))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Number: The total number of trials is fixed.
        self.lecture[3].set_color(COLOR_LIST)
        number_text = Text("Number (n=10)", font_size=32, color=COLOR_LIST)
        self.place_at_grid(number_text, "B4")
        self.play(FadeIn(number_text))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Success: The probability of success remains constant.
        self.lecture[4].set_color(COLOR_LIST)
        same_p_text = Text("Same p", font_size=32, color=COLOR_LIST)
        self.place_at_grid(same_p_text, "B5")
        
        # Fill slots sequentially with a mix of fish and X icons
        results = ["F", "X", "F", "F", "X", "F", "X", "F", "X", "F"]
        outcome_group = VGroup()
        for i, res in enumerate(results):
            row_idx = "D" if i < 5 else "E"
            col_idx = str((i % 5) + 1)
            if res == "F":
                m = get_fish()
            else:
                m = get_x()
            self.place_at_grid(m, f"{row_idx}{col_idx}")
            outcome_group.add(m)
            
        self.play(FadeIn(same_p_text))
        self.play(LaggedStart(*[FadeIn(m) for m in outcome_group], lag_ratio=0.2))
        self.wait(2)

        self.place_at_grid(n3sfs, "C4")
        self.place_at_grid(n3sff, "E4")
        self.place_at_grid(n3fss, "D4")
        self.place_at_grid(n3fsf, "F4")
        self.place_at_grid(n3ffs, "E5")
        self.place_at_grid(n3fff, "F5")
        
        # Edges
        edges_list = [
            Line(n0.get_center(), n1s.get_center(), color=WHITE),      # 0

            Line(n2fs.get_center(), n3fsf.get_center(), color=WHITE),  # 11
            Line(n2ff.get_center(), n3ffs.get_center(), color=WHITE),  # 12

        self.play(

            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===

        labels_group = VGroup(l_ssf, l_sfs, l_fss)
        bracket = Brace(labels_group, direction=RIGHT, color="#ADD8E6")
        
        ways_label = Text("3 ways to get 2 fish", font_size=16, color="#ADD8E6")
        self.place_at_grid(ways_label, "C6")
        
        comb_label = MathTex("3C2 = 3", color="#90EE90", font_size=32)
        self.place_at_grid(comb_label, "E6")

        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(Create(bracket), Write(ways_label))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===

        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(HIGHLIGHT_C))
        
        # Full formula: P(X=k) = \binom{n}{k} p^k (1-p)^{n-k}

        )

        self.wait(1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # p to the k represents the successes.
        self.play(

            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(BLUE_C),

            color=BLUE_C, 
            buff=0.1
        )
        self.play(Create(arrow_success), FadeIn(label_success))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # q to the n-minus-k represents the failures.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(CORAL_C),
            formula[4].animate.set_color(CORAL_C)
        )
        
        label_failure = Text("Failure Prob", font_size=20, color=CORAL_C)

from manim import *
import math

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Fetching data from storyboard
        title_text = "Visualizing the Distribution Shape"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Probability mass functions show the distribution of results.",
            "When p is low, the graph skews right.",
            "As p increases, the peak shifts to the right.",
            "High trial counts create a symmetric bell curve.",
            "This shape represents the most likely outcomes."
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)
        
        # Define constants and trackers
        chart_color = "#ADD8E6"
        highlight_color = YELLOW
        n_tracker = ValueTracker(10)
        p_tracker = ValueTracker(0.5)
        
        # Create Axes
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 31, 5],
            y_range=[0, 0.5, 0.1],
            x_length=5,
            y_length=4,
            axis_config={"include_tip": False}
        ).add_coordinates(font_size=14)
        self.place_in_area(axes, 'A1', 'F6', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Axis Labels
        x_label = Text("Number of Successes (k)", font_size=16, color=WHITE)
        x_label.next_to(axes.x_axis, DOWN, buff=0.4)
        y_label = Text("P(X=k)", font_size=16, color=WHITE).rotate(90*DEGREES)
        y_label.next_to(axes.y_axis, LEFT, buff=0.4)
        
        self.add(axes, x_label, y_label)

        # Create Bars
        bars = VGroup()
        for i in range(31):
            bar = Rectangle(
                width=0.12,
                height=0.01,
                fill_opacity=0.8,
                fill_color=chart_color,
                stroke_width=0.5,
                stroke_color=WHITE
            )
            bar.move_to(axes.c2p(i, 0), aligned_edge=DOWN)
            bars.add(bar)
            
        def update_bars(m):
            n = int(n_tracker.get_value())
            p = p_tracker.get_value()
            for i, b in enumerate(m):
                if i <= n:
                    # Binomial PMF: (n choose i) * p^i * (1-p)^(n-i)
                    try:
                        prob = math.comb(n, i) * (p**i) * ((1-p)**(n-i))
                    except:
                        prob = 0
                    
                    # Convert probability to visual height
                    target_height = axes.c2p(0, prob)[1] - axes.c2p(0, 0)[1]
                    # Update height using stretch_to_fit_height
                    b.stretch_to_fit_height(max(target_height, 0.001))
                    b.move_to(axes.c2p(i, 0), aligned_edge=DOWN)
                    b.set_opacity(0.8)
                else:
                    b.set_opacity(0)
                    
        bars.add_updater(update_bars)
        self.add(bars)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(highlight_color))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        skew_right_label = Text("Skewed Right", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(skew_right_label, 'B5', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(highlight_color),
            p_tracker.animate.set_value(0.2),
            Write(skew_right_label),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        skew_left_label = Text("Skewed Left", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(skew_left_label, 'B2', scale_factor=1.0)

        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(highlight_color),
            p_tracker.animate.set_value(0.8),
            ReplacementTransform(skew_right_label, skew_left_label),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(highlight_color),
            p_tracker.animate.set_value(0.5),
            n_tracker.animate.set_value(30),
            FadeOut(skew_left_label),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # For n=30, p=0.5, the mode is 15.
        highest_bar = bars[15]
        
        self.play(
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(highlight_color),
        )
        self.play(Flash(highest_bar, color=YELLOW, flash_radius=0.5, line_length=0.3))
        self.wait(2)
        
        # End state
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(1)

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Data
        title_text = "Real-World Application: Quality Control"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Binomial logic helps factories predict part defects.",
            "We calculate the likelihood of exceeding failure limits.",
            "Statistics ensures quality control in mass production."
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)
        
        # Colors
        c_white = "#FFFFFF"
        c_blue = "#ADD8E6"
        c_red = "#FF0000"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display a robot arm icon and a conveyor belt of gadgets in white #FFFFFF.
        
        # Conveyor
        belt = Line(LEFT * 1.0, RIGHT * 1.0, color=c_white, stroke_width=2)
        items = VGroup(*[Circle(radius=0.1, color=c_white, fill_opacity=1) for _ in range(4)])
        items.arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.3).shift(UP * 0.2)
        conveyor = VGroup(belt, items)
        
        # Robot Arm
        base = Rectangle(width=0.4, height=0.1, color=c_white, fill_opacity=1)
        arm_v = Rectangle(width=0.1, height=0.6, color=c_white, fill_opacity=1).next_to(base, UP, buff=0)
        arm_h = Rectangle(width=0.6, height=0.1, color=c_white, fill_opacity=1).next_to(arm_v, UP, buff=-0.05).shift(RIGHT*0.25)
        robot = VGroup(base, arm_v, arm_h)
        
        factory_viz = VGroup(conveyor, robot).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.4)
        self.place_in_area(factory_viz, "A1", "C3", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.lecture[0].set_color(c_white)
        self.play(Create(factory_viz), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Show the parameters 'n=50, p=0.02' next to the conveyor belt in light blue #ADD8E6.
        params = MathTex("n=50, \\ p=0.02", color=c_blue, font_size=36)
        self.place_at_grid(params, "C5", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.lecture[1].set_color(c_blue)
        self.play(Write(params))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Highlight the area of a distribution graph where X > 3 in red #FF0000 to represent 'Defect Risk'.
        
        # Manually defined binomial PMF values for n=50, p=0.02
        # k=0: 0.364, k=1: 0.371, k=2: 0.185, k=3: 0.061, k=4: 0.015, k=5: 0.003
        pmf_data = [0.364, 0.371, 0.185, 0.061, 0.015, 0.003, 0.001]
        
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 7, 1],
            y_range=[0, 0.5, 0.1],
            x_length=4,
            y_length=2.5,
            axis_config={"include_tip": False},
        ).scale(0.8)
        
        bars = VGroup()
        for k, val in enumerate(pmf_data):
            # Calculate height in units
            # y=0.5 is y_length (2.5)
            # so height = val * (2.5 / 0.5) = val * 5
            bar_height = val * 5 * 0.8 # scaled by axes scale
            bar = Rectangle(
                width=0.25,
                height=bar_height,
                fill_opacity=0.8,
                stroke_width=1
            )
            # Position at k
            bar.move_to(axes.c2p(k, val/2))
            
            if k > 3:
                bar.set_color(c_red)
                bar.set_fill(c_red)
            else:
                bar.set_color(c_white)
                bar.set_fill(c_white)
            bars.add(bar)
            
        risk_label = Text("Defect Risk (X > 3)", color=c_red, font_size=24)
        risk_label.next_to(axes, UP, buff=0.2)
        
        graph_group = VGroup(axes, bars, risk_label)
        self.place_in_area(graph_group, "D1", "F6", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        self.lecture[2].set_color(c_red)
        self.play(
            Create(axes),
            Create(bars),
            Write(risk_label),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(2)

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: The Bernoulli Trial", [
            "A Bernoulli trial has only two possible outcomes.",
            "We label these results as Success or Failure.",
            "The probability of success must stay the same."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show a card labeled 'Bernoulli Trial' in the center of the screen in white #FFFFFF.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        
        card_rect = RoundedRectangle(corner_radius=0.2, width=4, height=2, color=WHITE)
        card_text = Text("Bernoulli Trial", color=WHITE, font_size=36)
        card = VGroup(card_rect, card_text)
        self.place_in_area(card, 'B2', 'E5', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(card))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Split the screen: left side shows a fish icon 'Success (p=0.7)' in green #00FF00, 
        # right side shows 'Failure (q=0.3)' in red #FF0000.
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        
        # Success side (Left part of grid)
        # Using a simple shape for fish icon since no asset was provided
        success_icon = Triangle(color=GREEN).rotate(-90*DEGREES)
        success_label = Text("Success (p=0.7)", color=GREEN, font_size=24)
        success_group = VGroup(success_icon, success_label).arrange(DOWN)
        self.place_in_area(success_group, 'B1', 'E3', scale_factor=0.9)
        
        # Failure side (Right part of grid)
        failure_icon = Cross(stroke_width=6, color=RED)
        failure_label = Text("Failure (q=0.3)", color=RED, font_size=24)

        self.place_in_area(failure_group, 'B4', 'E6', scale_factor=0.9)

            FadeOut(card),

        p_label_highlight = Text("p=0.7", color=YELLOW, font_size=24)

        self.play(success_label.animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Fetching data from storyboard
        title_text = "Visualizing the Distribution Shape"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Probability mass functions show the distribution of results.",
            "When p is low, the graph skews right.",
            "As p increases, the peak shifts to the right.",
            "High trial counts create a symmetric bell curve.",
            "This shape represents the most likely outcomes."
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)
        
        # Define constants and trackers
        chart_color = "#ADD8E6"
        highlight_color = YELLOW
        n_tracker = ValueTracker(10)
        p_tracker = ValueTracker(0.5)
        
        # Create Axes
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 31, 5],
            y_range=[0, 0.5, 0.1],
            x_length=5,
            y_length=4,
            axis_config={"include_tip": False}
        ).add_coordinates(font_size=14)
        self.place_in_area(axes, 'A1', 'F6', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Axis Labels
        x_label = Text("Number of Successes (k)", font_size=16, color=WHITE)
        x_label.next_to(axes.x_axis, DOWN, buff=0.4)
        y_label = Text("P(X=k)", font_size=16, color=WHITE).rotate(90*DEGREES)
        y_label.next_to(axes.y_axis, LEFT, buff=0.4)
        
        self.add(axes, x_label, y_label)

        # Create Bars
        bars = VGroup()
        for i in range(31):
            bar = Rectangle(
                width=0.12,
                height=0.01,
                fill_opacity=0.8,
                fill_color=chart_color,
                stroke_width=0.5,
                stroke_color=WHITE
            )
            bar.move_to(axes.c2p(i, 0), aligned_edge=DOWN)
            bars.add(bar)
            
        def update_bars(m):
            n = int(n_tracker.get_value())
            p = p_tracker.get_value()
            for i, b in enumerate(m):
                if i <= n:
                    # Binomial PMF: (n choose i) * p^i * (1-p)^(n-i)
                    try:
                        prob = math.comb(n, i) * (p**i) * ((1-p)**(n-i))
                    except:
                        prob = 0
                    
                    # Convert probability to visual height
                    target_height = axes.c2p(0, prob)[1] - axes.c2p(0, 0)[1]
                    # Update height using stretch_to_fit_height
                    b.stretch_to_fit_height(max(target_height, 0.001))
                    b.move_to(axes.c2p(i, 0), aligned_edge=DOWN)
                    b.set_opacity(0.8)
                else:
                    b.set_opacity(0)
                    
        bars.add_updater(update_bars)
        self.add(bars)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(highlight_color))
        self.wait(2)

            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(highlight_color),
            p_tracker.animate.set_value(0.2),
            Write(skew_right_label),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        skew_left_label = Text("Skewed Left", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(skew_left_label, 'B2', scale_factor=1.0)

        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(highlight_color),
            p_tracker.animate.set_value(0.8),
            ReplacementTransform(skew_right_label, skew_left_label),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(2)

        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])

        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Fetching data from storyboard
        title_text = "Visualizing the Distribution Shape"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Probability mass functions show the distribution of results.",
            "When p is low, the graph skews right.",
            "As p increases, the peak shifts to the right.",
            "High trial counts create a symmetric bell curve.",
            "This shape represents the most likely outcomes."
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)
        
        # Define constants and trackers
        chart_color = "#ADD8E6"
        highlight_color = YELLOW
        n_tracker = ValueTracker(10)
        p_tracker = ValueTracker(0.5)
        
        # Create Axes
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 31, 5],
            y_range=[0, 0.5, 0.1],
            x_length=5,
            y_length=4,
            axis_config={"include_tip": False}
        ).add_coordinates(font_size=14)
        # Resolved Issue 36: Adjusted area and scale factor
        self.place_in_area(axes, 'B1', 'F6', scale_factor=0.7)
        
        # Axis Labels
        x_label = Text("Number of Successes (k)", font_size=16, color=WHITE)
        x_label.next_to(axes.x_axis, DOWN, buff=0.4)
        y_label = Text("P(X=k)", font_size=16, color=WHITE).rotate(90*DEGREES)
        y_label.next_to(axes.y_axis, LEFT, buff=0.4)
        
        self.add(axes, x_label, y_label)

        # Create Bars
        bars = VGroup()
        for i in range(31):
            bar = Rectangle(
                width=0.12,
                height=0.01,
                fill_opacity=0.8,
                fill_color=chart_color,
                stroke_width=0.5,
                stroke_color=WHITE
            )
            bar.move_to(axes.c2p(i, 0), aligned_edge=DOWN)
            bars.add(bar)
            
        def update_bars(m):
            n = int(n_tracker.get_value())
            p = p_tracker.get_value()
            for i, b in enumerate(m):
                if i <= n:
                    # Binomial PMF: (n choose i) * p^i * (1-p)^(n-i)
                    try:
                        # math.comb is safe for n <= 30
                        prob = math.comb(n, i) * (p**i) * ((1-p)**(n-i))
                    except:
                        prob = 0
                    
                    # Convert probability to visual height
                    target_height = axes.c2p(0, prob)[1] - axes.c2p(0, 0)[1]
                    # Update height using stretch_to_fit_height
                    b.stretch_to_fit_height(max(target_height, 0.001))
                    b.move_to(axes.c2p(i, 0), aligned_edge=DOWN)
                    b.set_opacity(0.8)
                else:
                    b.set_opacity(0)
                    
        bars.add_updater(update_bars)
        self.add(bars)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(highlight_color))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        skew_right_label = Text("Skewed Right", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        # Resolved Issue 34: Adjusted area and scale factor
        self.place_in_area(skew_right_label, 'A4', 'A6', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(highlight_color),
            p_tracker.animate.set_value(0.2),
            Write(skew_right_label),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        skew_left_label = Text("Skewed Left", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        # Resolved Issue 35: Adjusted area and scale factor
        self.place_in_area(skew_left_label, 'A1', 'A3', scale_factor=0.8)

        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(highlight_color),
            p_tracker.animate.set_value(0.8),
            ReplacementTransform(skew_right_label, skew_left_label),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(highlight_color),
            p_tracker.animate.set_value(0.5),
            n_tracker.animate.set_value(30),
            FadeOut(skew_left_label),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # For n=30, p=0.5, the mode is 15.
        highest_bar = bars[15]
        
        self.play(
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(highlight_color),
        )
        self.play(Flash(highest_bar, color=YELLOW, flash_radius=0.5, line_length=0.3))
        self.wait(2)
        
        # End state
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(1)

        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)

        chart_color = "#ADD8E6"
        highlight_color = YELLOW

        # Create Axes
        axes = Axes(

            y_range=[0, 0.5, 0.1],
            x_length=5,
            y_length=4,

        x_label.next_to(axes.x_axis, DOWN, buff=0.4)
        y_label = Text("P(X=k)", font_size=16, color=WHITE).rotate(90*DEGREES)
        y_label.next_to(axes.y_axis, LEFT, buff=0.4)
        
        self.add(axes, x_label, y_label)

        for i in range(31):

                stroke_width=0.5,

            bar.move_to(axes.c2p(i, 0), aligned_edge=DOWN)
            bars.add(bar)
            
        def update_bars(m):
            n = int(n_tracker.get_value())
            p = p_tracker.get_value()
            for i, b in enumerate(m):
                if i <= n:
                    # Binomial PMF calculation
                    try:
                        prob = math.comb(n, i) * (p**i) * ((1-p)**(n-i))
                    except:
                        prob = 0
                    
                    target_height = axes.c2p(0, prob)[1] - axes.c2p(0, 0)[1]
                    b.stretch_to_fit_height(max(target_height, 0.001))
                    b.move_to(axes.c2p(i, 0), aligned_edge=DOWN)
                    b.set_opacity(0.8)
                else:

        bars.add_updater(update_bars)
